item.title: China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint exercise opens in Vientiane
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
VIENTIANE, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- The China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise opened on Monday morning in the Lao capital Vientiane. The national anthems of China and Laos were first played at the ceremony. Chandy Soulivongsak, director general of the General Logistics Department of the Lao People's Army, and Wu Dan, head of the Chinese command and coordination group, then delivered speeches and announced the official start of the joint exercise. In his remarks, Chandy said that the Laos-China "Peace Train" joint exercise and medical service activities serve as a platform for enhancing the two militaries' capabilities in joint rescue and response to natural disasters, demonstrating the close and friendly relations between the two countries and militaries. He expressed confidence that the joint exercise would further deepen medical support cooperation between the two militaries. Also speaking at the ceremony, Wu said that the Chinese and Lao militaries have held this series of joint exercises six times since 2017. The return of the "Peace Train" medical team to Laos is not only a vivid practice of building an all-weather China-Laos community with a shared future in the new era, but also an important practice for deepening exchanges and cooperation between the two militaries in logistics and medical support. The exercise will run until late September, with more than 700 personnel from both sides participating. Set against the backdrop of international humanitarian medical rescue following a super typhoon disaster, the exercise features a three-tier command structure and a four-tier rescue system. Using medical trains, field medical treatment equipment and unmanned intelligent equipment, the two sides will organize mixed joint training, full-process joint rehearsals and live-force exercises. The exercise aims to explore operational models for cross-border joint medical rescue and further enhance the medical support coordination and emergency response capabilities of the two militaries. During the exercise, the two sides will also organize medical services and cultural exchange activities.

item.title: Japan urged to thoroughly destroy its chemical weapons abandoned in China: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A delegation from the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) has urged Japan to completely and thoroughly destroy its abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs) in China without further delay, according to the Chinese foreign ministry on Monday. The director-general of the OPCW, the chairperson of the Executive Council, as well as permanent representatives and senior diplomats from 12 countries to the OPCW, visited China upon invitation from Aug. 31 to Sept. 5, Mao Ning, a spokesperson for the ministry, said at a press briefing. During the visit, they travelled to Hunchun, Dunhua and Haerbaling in Jilin Province in northeast China to inspect the excavation, recovery and destruction of Japan's ACWs. Noting that the delegation's visit coincided with China's annual commemoration of the victory of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, Mao said Japan's militarist aggression inflicted immense humanitarian catastrophes on China and left behind the menace of ACWs. Through the visit, the delegation gained a deeper understanding of the grave harm posed by Japan's ACWs to the lives and property of the Chinese people and to the country's ecological environment, Mao said. They also expressed support for the OPCW, in accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, in urging the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its obligations by completely and thoroughly destroying its ACWs in China without further delay, so as to restore a safe habitat for the Chinese people at an early date and realize the noble goal of a world free of chemical weapons as envisaged by the Convention, she said.

item.title: Book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization published
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization has been published by the Higher Education Press and the People's Publishing House. Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has approached ecological conservation from the perspective of ensuring the sustainable development of the Chinese nation. With a profound understanding of the important position and strategic significance of ecological conservation in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era, the CPC Central Committee has vigorously advanced theoretical, practical and institutional innovation in this field, put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking and new strategies, led historic, transformative and comprehensive changes in China's ecological conservation, and developed Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization. The book introducing the thought, compiled under the organization of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee and the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, consists of an introduction and nine chapters, totaling about 170,000 Chinese characters. It systematically expounds on the significance, theoretical framework, essence, connotations and practical requirements of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization.

item.title: Asian coast guard high-level meeting to address non-traditional security challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
By Li Lei The upcoming 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies (HACGAM) High-Level Meeting will focus on non-traditional security challenges and ways to manage risks and crises amid a "complex and volatile" regional maritime security situation, a China Coast Guard spokesman said on Monday. The annual forum, set to open Tuesday in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, will also explore effective ways to promote cross-border cooperation and safeguard maritime peace and stability, spokesman Liu Dejun said. Liu noted that the meeting has evolved over more than two decades, expanding its membership to include countries and regions across East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia, and even some outside the region. Its institutional framework has grown increasingly robust, while cooperation has broadened into new areas. The organizing of HACGAM meetings follows China's chairing of the North Pacific Coast Guard Forum last year — an expansion from a six-nation "North Pacific Plus" event to a broader pan-Asia-Pacific forum. Liu said China remains committed to promoting its vision of a "maritime community with a shared future" and its Global Security Initiative, aiming to build consensus on regional maritime security governance. China hosted the HACGAM working-level meeting in May in Quanzhou, Fujian province, which provided technical support and outcomes that facilitated the opening of this week's high-level session.

item.title: China-Laos Peace Train 2026 Joint Humanitarian Medical Rescue Exercise to Be Held in Laos
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
BEIJING, Sept. 4 -- China-Laos Peace Train 2026 joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise will be held in Laos in September, said Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, on Friday. Taking international humanitarian medical rescue in a super typhoon disaster as its theme, the exercise focuses on such training subjects as joint on-site search and rescue, casualty evacuation, health and epidemic prevention, and psychological rescue. During the event, the Chinese side will also provide medical services for Lao military personnel and civilians. As the sixth exercise of this series, the joint exercise will further deepen and expand pragmatic exchange and cooperation in such fields as disaster medical rescue, tropical disease control and prevention, and infectious disease prevention and control, enhance the two militaries' capabilities in joint medical-service command, joint rescue, and joint prevention and control, and better provide quality public security goods for regional countries and peoples.
